summary:
Eleven phases (P0 to P10) run in order. P0, P1 and P2 are one PR each. From P3 onward every world ships in its own PR (`redesign/pNx-<world>`), and each trio of worlds shares one review Artifact. Every PR is squash-merged into `main` once the guard passes and the owner's pick is applied.

- **P0** changes nothing visible.
  - It moves every machine-facing element into contract includes (`_includes/contract/`). It turns `_layouts/default.html` into a dispatcher that picks each page's world from `_data/worlds/<id>.yml` (one file per world, all `legacy`). It makes `app-card.html` and `quick-answer.html` world-aware.
  - It adds `app:` to the 104 alternatives pages. It moves the hand-written /for/ hub, /guides/ hub and homepage FAQ lists into front matter, so one source feeds every renderer. It sets `theme: null`.
  - It ships the guard, capture, preview and promotion tooling under `scripts/redesign/`, plus three workflows: a PR guard on the real Pages builder, a non-blocking contract check on every push to `main`, and a post-deploy verify-live.
  - It records the current site's existing defects as an acknowledged baseline and commits Apple's official badge artwork.
- **P1** pilots one microsite end to end: Observa's app page, privacy page, support page and 8 alternatives pages. It proves the contract, the dispatcher, the shared block partials, the read-base layer and the whole selection loop before the large studio phase.
- **P2** ships the studio world (61 URLs) and adds the missing Guides link.
- **P3 to P8** ship the remaining apps in trios grouped by audience cluster and ordered by `ratings.count`. Each world has its own branch and PR.
  - body and recovery: GymLogger X, LiftLog, AfterShift
  - board games: Shogiful, Chessful, Xiangqiful
  - calm time: Taskful Day, Soon., EarnLock
  - money and records: AllPaid, RightSplit, Pawza
  - Mac developer tools: AppMeta, AppMeta Pulse, Mockly
  - media, reading and play: MediaKit, WanderWiki, Millrace
- **P9** ships Tare, which is unlisted and has no images yet. It may run in parallel any time after P1.
- **P10** removes style.css, animations.js, Inter/Newsreader and the legacy includes once nothing references them. It adds a studio fallback page for future apps, runs a finish review on every world, and writes DESIGN.md and a new CLAUDE.md design section.

Facts from the repo that the plan depends on (checked during this revision):
1. `head.html` only emits the Smart App Banner, the LCP image preload and `og:type=product` when `page.layout == "app"`. The plan keeps `layout: app`. The banner and `og:type` tests become `page.collection == "apps"`. Image preloads move into each world's head.
2. `llms.txt`, `ai-sitemap.xml`, the homepage and `/alternatives/` find and count comparison pages with `site.pages | where_exp: "p.url contains '/alternatives/'"`. So previews are built as separate full-site builds and assembled outside Jekyll. The generator templates read only `site.data.app_enrichment` and `site.data.transparency`, so new data files cannot change them.
3. There are 104 alternatives pages, not the 96 CLAUDE.md states. Each names its app only inside its body (`where: "slug", "<app>"`). Their comparison tables carry inline styles that use style.css tokens: about 1,600 `var(--s-3)`/`var(--s-4)` and 1,270 `var(--border-1)` references.
4. Only `app-card.html` (115 calls) and `quick-answer.html` (119 calls) are included from page bodies. Several hub lists are hand-written:
   - the `/alternatives/` index ItemList hard-codes `"numberOfItems": 104`;
   - the /for/ hub ItemList and cards, the /guides/ hub cards and the homepage FAQ are also written by hand.
5. Every page loads `lagerland-mark.png` (1.96 MB) through an absolute `{{ site.url }}` URL to show it at 30 px. App icons of 0.56–3.96 MB are shown at 40–64 px. The LCP hero image is a 0.7–3 MB PNG.
6. Production builds with github-pages 232: Jekyll 3.10.0 in safe mode, with jekyll-theme-primer as the default theme because `_config.yml` has no `theme:` key.
   - Built with the gem in the `:jekyll_plugins` group and a pinned `time:`, the current site is byte-identical to a Jekyll 4.4.1 build.
   - Outside that group, safe mode silently drops jekyll-sitemap and jekyll-redirect-from.
   - Dynamic include paths, include parameters and `static_files | where` work on 3.10.
   - Jekyll 4 filters such as `find` silently return their input on 3.10. All builds therefore use `liquid: strict_filters`, and all local builds use the production gem.
7. The current site already fails several absolute checks:
   - /guides/, /guides/best-xiangqi-apps-iphone/ and /apps/earnlock/terms/ cannot be reached from /;
   - 94 pages show star glyphs, while 0 pages have `aggregateRating`;
   - review measurements found the quick answer below 1.5 viewports at 390 on 4 apps, the badge outside the first viewport on Millrace and EarnLock, and horizontal overflow on MediaKit.
   So the guard compares head against base everywhere, and applies absolute rules only to pages whose world is live.
8. From this cloud session, the egress proxy blocks both the live site and the Pages REST API (CONNECT 403 and HTTP 403). GitHub Actions data is readable through the GitHub MCP tools, including the `pages-build-deployment` workflow (id 227213120). Post-deploy checks therefore run in Actions and are read through MCP.
architecture:
## 1. Rules the architecture keeps
- **No changes to URLs or front-matter meaning.** Permalinks, layout names (`default`, `app`, `journal`, `privacy`, `support`) and every existing key keep their meaning.
  - P0 adds only keys lifted from each page's own body, and the rendered output stays identical:
    - `app: <slug>` on the 104 alternatives pages;
    - `items:` on `for/index.html` and `guides/index.html`;
    - `faq:` on `index.html`;
    - `for_apps:` on the 4 audience pages.
  - The redesign never edits `_apps/*.md` (the ratings bot owns those files), the `_journal/*.md` bodies (they feed `feed.xml`), or `_data/{transparency,testimonials,app_enrichment}.yml`.
  - It adds `_data/worlds/<id>.yml` and `_data/derivatives.yml`. No generator template reads them.
  - It adds `theme: null` to `_config.yml`. Without it, deleting style.css in P10 would let Primer's `style.scss` take over the same URL.
- **Machine-facing output comes only from layouts and contract includes, never from a world.** That covers `<head>`, every JSON-LD block, microdata, speakable targets and the generated files.
  - A lint stops any world `head.html` from emitting title, description, robots, canonical, OG, Twitter or `apple-itunes-app` tags, or `ld+json`.
- **Every front-matter block renders.** Section order, grouping and form belong to the world, but every block present in front matter must appear.
  - The world renders a block either with its own partial or with the shared `contract/blocks/<key>.html`, and the element always carries `data-block="<key>"`.
  - Each contract include marks its root with `data-contract="<name>"`.
- **Content stays where authors edit it.** Hand-written bodies are not rewritten: the 104 alternatives pages, the /alternatives/ index, 5 guides, 4 audience pages, about, /support/, the app sub-pages and the journal markdown.
  - Only bodies that are really layouts move into templates: home, `/apps/`, `/journal/`, the /for/ and /guides/ hubs, and transparency.
  - Their lists render from front matter (`items:`, `faq:`) or from collections, so an author still edits one place.
  - `check-contract.py` fails a PR, and `contract-main.yml` flags a push, if any of these pages gains body content again.
- **One file per world.** `_data/worlds/<id>.yml` holds `status: legacy | preview | shipped`, plus `handles:` (the block keys the world designed itself) and `contrast_pairs:`. Separate files mean per-world PRs never conflict, and the status field doubles as the rollback switch.

## 2. World resolution: `_includes/contract/resolve-world.html`
The resolver assigns only `w_`-prefixed variables, because include assigns leak into the caller. It uses nested `if`s, with no `not`, no parentheses and one `and`/`or` per condition, since Liquid evaluates `and`/`or` right to left and silently mis-parses parentheses.
```liquid
{%- assign w_id = 'studio' -%}{%- assign w_mode = 'read' -%}
{%- if page.collection == 'apps' -%}
  {%- assign w_id = page.slug -%}{%- assign w_mode = 'persuade' -%}
{%- elsif page.app -%}
  {%- assign w_id = page.app -%}
{%- else -%}
  {%- assign w_parts = page.url | split: '/' -%}
  {%- if w_parts[1] == 'apps' and w_parts.size > 3 -%}
    {%- assign w_id = w_parts[2] -%}
  {%- elsif w_parts[1] == 'alternatives' and w_parts.size > 2 -%}
    {%- assign w_id = '' -%}
  {%- elsif page.url == '/' -%}
    {%- assign w_mode = 'persuade' -%}
  {%- endif -%}
{%- endif -%}
{%- assign w_conf = site.data.worlds[w_id] -%}
{%- assign w_live = false -%}
{%- unless site.force_legacy -%}
  {%- if w_conf.status == 'shipped' -%}
    {%- assign w_live = true -%}
  {%- elsif w_conf.status == 'preview' -%}
    {%- if site.preview_style -%}{%- assign w_live = true -%}{%- endif -%}
  {%- endif -%}
{%- endunless -%}
```
- **What the branches cover:**
  - `/apps/<slug>/<sub>/` covers privacy, support, methodology, coaches, terms and api-access.
  - An alternatives page with no `app:` resolves to `''`, which means legacy until P10. From P10 on it uses the studio read frame, and `contract-main.yml` opens an issue.
- **Template choice.** `w_tpl` is assigned the same way (`page`, `privacy`, `support`, `read`, `home`, `hub-apps`, `hub-journal`, `hub-for`, `hub-guides`, `post`, `article`, `transparency`).
- **Paths.**
  - Shipped: `w_dir = worlds/<id>` and `w_asset = /assets/worlds/<id>/<id>`.
  - Candidate: `w_dir = worlds/<id>/<site.preview_style>` and `w_asset = /assets/worlds/<id>/<site.preview_style>`.
- **Which config sets what.**
  - `site.preview_style` is set only by `scripts/redesign/config/style-{a,b,c}.yml`.
  - `site.force_legacy` is set only by `config/force-legacy.yml`.
  - `site.resolver_debug` is set only by `config/resolver-debug.yml`. It makes the contract head emit `<meta name="lagerland-world" content="id|mode|tpl|dir">` for the fixture tests.
- **Safety.** GitHub Pages builds with plain `_config.yml`, so a branch that carries candidates still renders `legacy` there, and an unselected style cannot reach production by mistake.

## 3. Layouts
- **`_layouts/default.html` becomes the dispatcher.**
  - Live world: `<html class="w-{{w_id}}">`, then `contract/head.html`, then `{% include {{ w_dir }}/head.html %}`. The world head holds theme-color, color-scheme, at most 2 font preloads, the stylesheets, its own LCP image preload, and its JS with `defer`. Then `contract/skip-link.html`, then `{% include {{ w_dir }}/{{ w_tpl }}.html body=content %}`, then `contract/footer-strip.html` (app worlds only), then `/assets/js/contract.js` with `defer`.
  - Otherwise: `{% include legacy/document.html body=content %}`, which is today's markup verbatim.
- **`_layouts/app.html` keeps its name.**
  - It always includes `contract/app-schema.html` first. That file holds SoftwareApplication with Offer/AggregateOffer, `aggregateRating` only when count ≥ 25, FAQPage, BreadcrumbList, HowTo, CreativeWork and the founder Person/Organization, all moved verbatim from today's `app.html`.
  - Then it renders either `{{ w_dir }}/page.html`, followed by `contract/blocks/rest.html` and `contract/sticky-bar.html`, or `legacy/app-body.html`.
- **`journal.html`, `privacy.html` and `support.html`** work the same way, with `contract/journal-schema.html` (Article, FAQPage and Breadcrumb, with speakable `.quick-answer__body` and `.faq-a`).
- **Head conditions.**
  - In `contract/head.html`, the Smart App Banner and `og:type` tests become `page.collection == "apps"`, which matches exactly the same pages.
  - Both image preloads (the per-app first screenshot, and `/assets/screenshots/observa/1.png` on `/`) leave the contract.
  - `legacy/assets.html` keeps them byte for byte with today's tests. Each world head preloads only its own derivative, using `imagesrcset`/`imagesizes`.
- **Never create `_layouts/redirect.html`.** jekyll-redirect-from would start using it for its stubs.

## 4. Contract includes (`_includes/contract/`)
Each is listed with its marker and what it emits or computes.
- `head.html` emits:
  - title (`seo.title` or `title`), meta description, author, publisher, robots, keywords, icons, canonical and hreflang;
  - the alternate links to the feed, `ai-index.json`, `llms`, `llms-full` and the sitemaps, plus `rel=me`;
  - all OG and Twitter tags, the Organization and WebSite JSON-LD with computed counts, the Smart App Banner, the inline `html.js` line, and GoatCounter.

  Preview builds (`site.preview`) instead emit `noindex,nofollow` and `<meta name="lagerland-preview">`, and leave out GoatCounter.
- **Schema includes:** `app-schema.html`, `journal-schema.html` and `schema/{home,apps,for,guides,journal}.html`.
  - Hub ItemLists and the home FAQPage render from collections or from the page's own `items:`/`faq:`, so JSON-LD and visible lists share one source.
  - The `/alternatives/` index keeps its JSON-LD and cards in its body. Its `numberOfItems` is computed with the `where_exp` the page already uses for its visible count.
- `quick-answer.html` (`quick-answer`): `.quick-answer__body` (`itemprop=text`) plus the speakable WebPage JSON-LD. The label text is a parameter.
- `ai-canonical.html` (`ai-canonical`): the "Quick reference" `<details>` block, verbatim. It may be restyled or moved, never hidden.
- `badge.html` (`badge`): Apple's official artwork (`/assets/badges/app-store-badge-en-black.svg`, `img` 120×40 or larger, alt "Download on the App Store"), inside an `<a>` to `app_store_url` with an aria-label. Size is a parameter. It carries `data-sticky-sentinel` when used as the hero action.
- `qr.html` (`qr`) renders only when two things are true:
  - `platforms` includes an iPhone or iPad platform (`iOS`, `iPadOS`, `iPhone` or `iPad`; Tare uses the last two);
  - `/assets/qr/<slug>.svg` exists in `site.static_files`.

  It shows at a minimum of 96 px and is never inverted or filtered. Mac-only AppMeta and Mockly get no QR, because scanning would land an iPhone on a listing it cannot install.
- `sticky-bar.html` (`sticky-bar`), `price.html` (`price`) and `rating.html` (`rating`): as before. The rating stays silent until `ratings.count` ≥ 25, then matches the schema.
- `privacy-proof.html` (`privacy-proof`) shows the `privacy.*` fields and links to `/apps/<slug>/privacy/` and `/apps/<slug>/support/`. The `_data/transparency.yml` row data and the `/transparency/#<slug>` link render only when a row for the slug exists. Tare has none.
- `maker.html` (`maker`): "Built by Lagerland Apps" with Organization microdata, last updated, first released, version, the backstory link and the email.
- `footer-strip.html` (`footer-strip`) is the only element shared across microsites. "A Lagerland app" links to:
  - home, all apps, `/alternatives/`;
  - the app's audience page(s) under `/for/`, computed from the `for_apps:` lists;
  - transparency, and the app's privacy policy and support.

  It reads the host world's `--strip-*` tokens and body face, plus the Lagerland mark derivative. It has no studio-specific styling, so the pilot needs no retrofit.
- **Blocks.** `blocks/<key>.html` is a shared semantic renderer for every known front-matter block key: faq, how_it_works (with `#how-it-works` and step ids), comparison_table, plans/pricing, release_notes, roadmap, spotlight, value_points, features, who_for, testimonials, plateau_disclosure, training_vocabulary, coach_cta, insight_gallery, example_insights, value_math, related_journal, alternatives_to, screenshots, founder and show_body.
  - A world styles these or overrides them with its own partial, which keeps `data-block`.
  - `blocks/rest.html` renders, before the maker line, every known key present in front matter but missing from the world's `handles:`. A block added on `main` later therefore always renders.
- **Resolvers** assign variables and emit nothing:
  - `resolve-world.html`;
  - `alt-links.html`: `w_alt_links` and `w_alt_primary`, with the `alt_pairs` and `comparison_slugs` maps moved verbatim from `_includes/alternatives.html`;
  - `related.html`;
  - `derivative.html`: looks up `site.data.derivatives[src]` and falls back to the original `src`.
- **The two body-called includes stay as shims.** `_includes/app-card.html` and `_includes/quick-answer.html` keep their paths. Each renders the world version when the page's world is live, and today's markup verbatim otherwise.
- **Required IDs.** `#how-it-works` must exist whenever `how_it_works.steps` does. `#faq`, `#pricing` and `#features` are required whenever a link or JSON-LD URL targets them.

## 5. File layout
Phase time (candidates):
```
_data/worlds/observa.yml     {status: preview, scheme: dark, handles: [...], contrast_pairs: [...], candidates: {a: {label, kicker}, b: …, c: …}}
_includes/worlds/observa/{a,b,c}/   head.html page.html read.html privacy.html support.html app-card.html _*.html
assets/worlds/observa/{a,b,c}.css  (+ a.js only for a signature interaction)
assets/fonts/<fontsource-id>/…woff2 + LICENSE        (shared pool, fonts.lock.json)
assets/img/d/<sha8>-{360,720,1080}.webp, assets/img/d/<sha8>-{64,128,256}.webp   (content-hashed derivatives)
_data/derivatives.yml        '/assets/screenshots/observa/1.png': {sha256, w: [360,720,1080], base: /assets/img/d/<sha8>}
```
Shipped (after `promote-winner.py`):
```
_includes/worlds/observa/*.html   assets/worlds/observa/observa.css (+ observa.js)
_data/worlds/observa.yml  {status: shipped, scheme, handles, contrast_pairs, label, picked: 2026-11-03}
```
- Partials are included through `{{ w_dir }}` and assets through `{{ w_asset }}`, so promotion is a move plus deletions, with no rewriting.
- The studio uses `_includes/worlds/studio/` (head, persuade, read, home, hub-apps, hub-journal, hub-for, hub-guides, post, article, transparency, app-card) and `assets/worlds/studio/studio.css`.

## 6. CSS
- **`assets/css/contract.css`** (≤ 1.5 KB gz) holds mechanics only:
  - badge sizes;
  - the QR media rule `(min-width:900px) and (hover:hover) and (pointer:fine)`;
  - the sticky bar (hidden without `html.js`, transform toggle, no transition under reduced motion);
  - `html.js [data-reveal]`, `.visually-hidden`, the skip link, and `scroll-padding` fed by `--sticky-h`.

  It sets no colour and no font.
- **`assets/css/read-base.css`** (≤ 3.5 KB gz, loaded on read pages of live worlds only) is token-only structure for the legacy body vocabulary and for the shared block partials. It contains no colour or font values, only `var()` references to world semantic tokens.
  - It covers every class in `legacy-classes.txt` (about 100: `hero`, `overline`, `lead`, `gradient-text`, `section*`, `grid-*`, `card*`, `faq*`, `btn*`, `compare-*`, `kv*`, `pill`, `prose`, `privacy-block`, …).
  - It defines every inline token in `legacy-tokens.txt` (`--s-2` to `--s-5`, `--border-1`, `--border-2`, `--text-sm`, …) mapped onto world tokens. Inline `style=` attributes in comparison tables therefore keep their padding and rules in every world.
  - Banned forms are restyled, never deleted: `gradient-text` becomes plain ink, and `overline` becomes inline meta text.
  - An accessibility fix to body vocabulary is one edit, not 21.
- **One world stylesheet per page:** `assets/worlds/<w>/<w>.css`. It covers persuade and read, holds the tokens on `.w-<id>`, and follows the world's scene: a single scheme sets `color-scheme`, a pair is designed in both.
- **Vocabulary changes.** `scan-classes.py` writes `legacy-classes.txt` and `legacy-tokens.txt` from bodies and inline styles.
  - A listed class or token missing from read-base is a FAIL.
  - A class or token that newly appears in a body (for example, from another session's page) is a WARN that the owner resolves: style it in read-base or rewrite the body. It is never a 21-world failure.
- **`assets/css/style.css` is frozen from P0.** Only `legacy/assets.html` loads it, and P10 deletes it.

## 7. Fonts
- `scripts/redesign/fetch-font.sh <fontsource-id> <weights> [italic] [--variable]` runs `npm pack` in scratch. It copies the latin `woff2` files and the LICENSE into `assets/fonts/<id>/`, and records version, files and sha256 in `fonts.lock.json`.
- Each world declares its `@font-face` rules (`font-display: swap`, latin `unicode-range`) and a metric-matched fallback face (computed by `font-metrics.py`, using fontTools). It preloads at most 2 files.
- Budget: 160 KB of woff2 per page at most. Shared families share one cached file. Inter and Newsreader stay for legacy pages until P10.

## 8. JS
- `assets/js/contract.js` (≤ 1.5 KB gz) does three things:
  - toggles the sticky bar from `[data-sticky-sentinel]`;
  - sets `--sticky-h`;
  - runs the `[data-reveal]` observer with the 2.5 s force-visible safety net.
- A world may add `<w>.js` (≤ 5 KB gz, `defer`) for its signature interaction. The server-rendered state is the fallback, and the script is inert under reduced motion.
- `animations.js` stays for legacy pages. P0 gives it the `[data-sticky-sentinel]` selector, with `.hero .actions` as the fallback.

## 9. Images and video
- **Derivatives.** `make-derivatives.py` (uv + Pillow) writes WebP derivatives with content-hashed names:
  - screenshots at 360, 720 and 1080 widths;
  - icons at 64, 128 and 256 px;
  - the Lagerland mark at 64 and 128 px.

  It records `_data/derivatives.yml`, keyed by the source path and holding the source's sha256.
- **Lookup.** Templates resolve each `src` through `contract/derivative.html`. A source with no entry (a new or renamed screenshot) falls back to the original PNG, so it is never wrong, only heavier.
- **Staleness.** A file replaced in place cannot be detected at build time (Liquid cannot hash files). `contract-main.yml` runs `make-derivatives.py --check` on every push and reports stale or missing entries.
- **Video.** WanderWiki's video derivatives (MP4, WebM, poster) are entries keyed by the `.mov` path in `hero.video`, never hard-coded in a world.
- **Markup.** Images use `srcset`/`sizes`, width and height, and `fetchpriority=high` on the LCP image only. JSON-LD `screenshot`/`image` and `og:image` keep the original URLs.

## 10. Read variants
- Privacy, support and the app-owned sub-pages (`aftershift/methodology`, `gymlogger-x/coaches`, `earnlock/terms`, `appmeta-pulse/api-access`) get their world from the URL.
- Alternatives pages get it from `app:`, which P0's codemod `tag-alternatives.py` adds from each body's `where: "slug"`. An untagged page stays legacy (until P10) rather than wearing the wrong world.
- The world's `read.html` owns the frame. The reading column stays calm.

## 11. Generated files and redirects
- `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, `ai-index.json`, `ai-sitemap.xml`, `feed.xml`, `sitemap.xml`, `sitemap_index.xml`, `robots.txt`, `humans.txt`, `.well-known/*` and `redirects.json` are `layout: none` templates or plugin output, so the redesign cannot change them. The guard requires them byte-identical under the pinned `time:`.
- Redirect stubs:
  - 5 come from jekyll-redirect-from: `/apps/calm-2048/` and `/apps/zen-2048/` (from `_apps/millrace.md`), and `/apps/screenflow-studio/` with its `privacy/` and `support/` (from Mockly's pages). `redirects.json` lists 8 keys because it also includes the `index.html` variants.
  - `/apps/thewait/` is a hand-written `layout: null` stub.
  - All 6 must stay byte-identical, and no `redirect_from` key is touched.

## 12. Engines
- **Local builds** all run through `scripts/redesign/jekyll.sh`:
  - the github-pages 232 bundle from `scripts/redesign/ci/Gemfile` (`gem 'github-pages', group: :jekyll_plugins`, lockfile committed);
  - run with that folder as the working directory and `-s <src> -d <out> --safe`;
  - `BUNDLE_PATH` in scratch (never under the repo, since `exclude:` replaces Jekyll's defaults);
  - `LANG=C.UTF-8` (Primer's Sass fails under a POSIX locale) and `JEKYLL_ENV=production`;
  - overlays `config/local.yml` (`baseurl: ""`, which stops github-metadata's blocked API call) and `config/parity.yml` (`time: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"`, `liquid: {strict_filters: true}`).
- **CI** uses `actions/jekyll-build-pages@v1`, the real Pages builder, with `GITHUB_TOKEN`. A CI-only step appends the parity keys to each checkout's `_config.yml`; nothing is committed.
- **Template lint** rejects `find`, `find_exp`, `{% render %}`, `not`, and parentheses or mixed `and`/`or` in conditions.

## 13. Drift after shipping (`.github/workflows/contract-main.yml`)
It runs `on: push` to `main`, is non-blocking, and keeps one tracking issue up to date. It runs:
- pages-compat;
- `check-contract.py` absolute rules on every live-world URL (every block key present renders `data-block` with its leaf text visible; markers; required ids);
- the `app:` check on alternatives pages;
- the check that relocated hubs have empty bodies;
- the derivative staleness check;
- an unknown-block-key report for `_apps/*.md`.

This covers launches and edits that go straight to `main` under CLAUDE.md, and the ratings bot's commits.

## 14. Rollback and future apps
- Until P10, setting `status: legacy` in one world file is a one-line revert. After P10, use `git revert` of the world's squash commit (a new commit, never a history rewrite).
- P10 adds `_includes/worlds/studio/app-fallback/`: a full-contract page in the studio's style for any future app that has no world yet.

## Previews are not Jekyll pages
Rendering `/preview/<slug>/<a|b|c>/` inside a Jekyll build has three problems:
- the llms and sitemap lists and the hub counts would pick up the preview copies;
- safe mode allows no generator plugin, so it would mean committing stub files;
- the copies would carry wrong canonicals.

Instead, every candidate renders at its real URL in its own full-site build, and the review pages are assembled outside Jekyll. `/preview/` paths exist only inside the private Artifact.

## Candidate builds (`scripts/redesign/preview-build.sh pN`)

risks: After this phase, per-world rollback is no longer one line. Mitigation: wait 14 days or more; git revert of a world's squash commit stays available.
Hidden references to style.css or animations.js in content bodies. Mitigation: grep the built site and source before deleting; verify-live checks every referenced asset returns 200.

risks.risk: A microsite leaves out a contract element or a front-matter block, or moves the quick answer down the page.
risks.mitigation: Layouts emit all schema and head output. blocks/rest.html renders every known block a world did not handle. check-contract.py requires the markers and data-block elements. The capture checks fail when the quick answer sits below 1.5 viewports or the badge is outside the first viewport.

risks.risk: Content is silently dropped or hidden by CSS when a world reorganises a page, especially on the mobile render Google indexes.
risks.mitigation: Coverage is checked three ways against base: front-matter leaves by key path, text blocks, and rendered visibility at 390 and 1440 with details opened. The rendered check also fails on clipped and visually-hidden text, and the JS-off text must equal the JS-on text.

risks.risk: The guard passes vacuously because CI used a different engine or skipped plugins (no sitemap, no redirects on either side).
risks.mitigation: CI builds with actions/jekyll-build-pages. Local builds use the github-pages bundle in the :jekyll_plugins group. Sanity assertions require every generated file and stub, and a file missing from both builds is a FAIL. P0 requires the local and CI digests to match.

risks.risk: Local and production engines diverge (a Jekyll 4 filter that silently misbehaves on 3.10).
risks.mitigation: Every build runs on github-pages 232 with liquid strict_filters, and lint-templates.py rejects find, find_exp, render, not and parenthesised conditions. The owner approves exactly what Pages renders.

risks.risk: Rules that the current site already breaks make every gate unpassable, or get waved through.
risks.mitigation: Every URL is compared with base. Absolute rules apply only where a world is live. The current site's defects are committed in baseline/incumbent.json, approved once, and each is scheduled for a fix (Guides in P2, EarnLock terms in P5, Millrace and MediaKit in P8).

risks.risk: Edits pushed straight to main after a world ships (new blocks, new alternatives pages, new screenshots, new body classes) bypass the PR guard and drift silently.
risks.mitigation: contract-main.yml runs on every push to main (non-blocking, one tracking issue). It checks block rendering, app: tags, relocated-hub bodies, derivative staleness and vocabulary. Block fallbacks render new keys, untagged alternatives stay legacy, and derivative lookups fall back to originals.

risks.risk: Hand-written hub lists end up in several copies (contract schema, legacy body, studio template, a/b/c candidates), and launches update only one.
risks.mitigation: The /for/ and /guides/ hubs and the home FAQ render from one front-matter list. The /alternatives/ index keeps its body and computes numberOfItems. CLAUDE.md gets a where-things-moved table in P0, and relocated pages that regain body content are flagged.

risks.risk: Post-deploy verification cannot run from the session (the proxy blocks the live site and the Pages API).
risks.mitigation: verify-live.yml runs in GitHub Actions after pages-build-deployment. Claude reads both runs through the GitHub MCP tools and dispatches verify-live if workflow_run does not fire.

risks.risk: Microsites lose the sitewide studio footer links, which weakens internal linking.
risks.mitigation: The footer strip links /alternatives/ and the app's /for/ pages, and the studio footer links every live app. The link graph fails new orphans and depth increases relative to base. Inbound changes come as one aggregated table per PR.

risks.risk: A preview or candidate style leaks into production, or into the llms and sitemap lists.
risks.mitigation: Previews are separate builds assembled outside Jekyll. Candidates need site.preview_style, which only local configs set. The leak check looks for dedicated markers (data-review-bar, /preview/ paths, lagerland-preview and lagerland-world metas). check-clean.py runs before the PR is ready, and squash merges keep losing styles out of main's history.

risks.risk: The ratings-sync bot pushes daily, so branches go stale.
risks.mitigation: The redesign never edits _apps/*.md. Branches merge origin/main and are never rebased or force-pushed. CI builds the merge ref, so diffs isolate the branch's own changes.

risks.risk: Each world's fonts, screenshots and preloads push performance below the current site's.
risks.mitigation: Hard budgets per page. Derivatives replace the 1–4 MB PNGs. Image preloads moved out of the contract head, so no world preloads the unused legacy PNG, and unused preloads fail.

risks.risk: Sameness: 20 microsites become one template in different costumes, made more likely by the shared block partials and read-base.
risks.mitigation: The partials are semantic only, and worlds own order, grouping, form and overrides. Dice-protocol style cards, sibling trios decided together in the siblings view, and a finish review comparing section order, navigation, type and signature interaction.

risks.risk: Candidate gating cost: 63 world implementations, 42 discarded, each through an ~18-render matrix.
risks.mitigation: Two tiers: candidates pass cheap static rules plus a quick capture of representative pages; the full matrix, vitals, axe on every URL and VoiceOver run only on winners. Trios split into per-world PRs.

risks.risk: Owner decisions are slow or absent.
risks.mitigation: One bounded revision round. A world without a pick is deferred while the rest of the trio ships. Picks are recorded in the Artifact database and confirmed in chat.

risks.risk: Rankings or CTR drop after a world ships.
risks.mitigation: GSC review at 7 and 28 days against out-of-scope control pages. Before P10 the rollback is one line (status: legacy); after it, git revert of the world's squash commit.

risks.risk: Inline styles in 104 alternatives bodies depend on style.css tokens, so tables lose padding and rules in new worlds.
risks.mitigation: scan-classes.py emits legacy-tokens.txt. read-base.css defines every token mapped onto world tokens, check-contract enforces it, and a computed-style check confirms it on comparison tables. An optional content pass to replace inline styles is left to the owner.

risks.risk: Artifact limits break the review.
risks.mitigation: Chunked publishes to one Artifact URL (≤ 255 files and 64 MB per publish, ≤ 511 files and 256 MB per version). Current is shown as captures, assets are de-duplicated by hash, and derivatives are used.

risks.risk: Committed derivatives and fonts grow the repo.
risks.mitigation: Derivatives only for in-scope apps (WebP, 3 widths, content-hashed). Shared fonts, with orphans pruned on promotion. Expected growth is about 20–30 MB against roughly 250 MB of assets today.

risks.risk: IndexNow resubmits the whole sitemap on every phase merge (_includes, _layouts and _data are global triggers), which IndexNow discourages.
risks.mitigation: Squash commits carry [skip indexnow]. After verify-live passes, indexnow.yml is dispatched with only the in-scope URLs. P0 submits nothing.

risks.risk: The current App Store badge is an approximation drawn with system fonts, which is arguably a redraw of Apple artwork.
risks.mitigation: Apple's official SVG is a P0 exit criterion (committed unused) and goes live in P1 through contract/badge.html. CSS lint forbids altering it.
